Pairings

Why this plate with this glass.

NASHA designs food and drink together. Each of the five core dishes has a beer, and a zero-proof drink of equal standing, chosen for a reason you can taste and argue with.

The reasons are simple: a cold, clean drink calms chile; something bright cuts richness; a shared aroma links plate and glass; a bitter edge can grip fat but can also sharpen heat. Each pairing names how it could go wrong and the small tasting that will decide it.

Concept stage: there is no brewery, no restaurant, no truck and no menu for sale. Images are concept visualizations and illustrations, not photographs of NASHA. The pairings are proposed and not sensory tested; none has a score.

The ideas, in plain words.

  • Cleansing. Resets the mouth between bites.
  • Contrast. Opposite qualities that balance each other.
  • Aroma Bridge. A shared smell that links food and drink.
  • Acidity. Brightness that cuts richness.
  • Sweetness. Sweetness that softens heat.
  • Heat Relief. Cold and low bitterness that calm chile.
  • Texture. Bubbles or body that answer the dish's texture.
  • Bitterness. Bitterness that grips fat (and can sharpen heat).
  • Roast. Toasty notes that echo char.
  • Spice. Spice in the glass that echoes spice on the plate.

The five pairings.

Chicken 65 Totopos

IN DEVELOPMENT

Beer, first idea
Mexican-Style Lager
Zero-proof, first idea
An agua-fresca-style drink of fruit, lime and a little salt: bright, acidic and lightly savory, served very cold.

cleansingcontrastheat reliefacidity

Why it may work. The beer is light and low in bitterness, so it should refresh against fried, medium-heat chicken without adding to the chile. The fruit-and-acid drink does the same job with lime and salt.

Alternates, how it could fail, what decides it
Beer, alternate
Pilsner
Zero-proof, alternate
A chilled, lightly sweetened tea with spiced citrus; tannin and citrus give a dry, refreshing edge without heat.

How it could fail. A light lager could be too thin for the fat. A bitter pilsner or tannic tea could add to the chile burn. A sweet drink could feel heavy beside fried food.

What decides it. Taste each drink beside the same chicken and chip at the start and after ten minutes, then ask whether the heat, fat and chip crunch feel better or worse.

Paneer Tikka Taco

IN DEVELOPMENT

Beer, first idea
Witbier
Zero-proof, first idea
A spiced-citrus drink with a gentle herbal edge and light sparkle that echoes lime and cilantro.

aroma bridgeaciditycleansingcontrast

Why it may work. Citrus and herbal aroma should link to the cilantro, lime and char, and the acidity cuts the paneer's richness. The NA drinks aim at the same bridge.

Alternates, how it could fail, what decides it
Beer, alternate
Mexican-Style Lager
Zero-proof, alternate
A hop-water-style botanical drink, dry and aromatic, with citrus peel and no sweetness.

How it could fail. Coriander and citrus against the cilantro or lime could taste soapy to some guests. A strongly spiced drink could compete with the marinade.

What decides it. Taste the beer and both NA drinks with the same taco, with and without cilantro, and note any soapy or clashing flavours.

Goat Birria, Sealed-Pot Braise

IN DEVELOPMENT

Beer, first idea
Hefeweizen
Zero-proof, first idea
A tea-based drink with tamarind or hibiscus acid and warm spice, served cool or slightly warm, matching the dish's chile and cinnamon notes.

contrastaroma bridgeaciditytexturebitterness

Why it may work. Carbonation, acid and tannin cut the fat in the consomme, and warm spice in the drink can echo the adobo. The amber style bridges toasty malt to the braise.

Alternates, how it could fail, what decides it
Beer, alternate
Vienna Amber
Zero-proof, alternate
A non-alcoholic beer with a malty, toasty, gentle-bodied character (a brewer or supplier to define; strength and labelling to be confirmed) to answer the braise.

How it could fail. Clove and banana against the dish's clove and cinnamon is a gamble. A malty option could be heavy with a rich consomme. Too much sweetness would clog.

What decides it. Taste the same goat portion with each option, alternating with the consomme, and note which one leaves the palate cleaner after a few bites.

Gobi Taco

IN DEVELOPMENT

Beer, first idea
Pilsner
Zero-proof, first idea
A lime-forward agua-fresca-style drink with a pinch of salt and a little green herb, cold and crisp.

contrastcleansingaciditybitterness

Why it may work. Crisp carbonation and light bitterness should reset the palate between bites of roasted, glazed cauliflower, and the lime and saline drinks echo the slaw and pickle.

Alternates, how it could fail, what decides it
Beer, alternate
Mexican-Style Lager
Zero-proof, alternate
A savory, saline drink with tamarind and a light spice, a nod to chaat flavours, kept thin and not sweet.

How it could fail. Bitterness beside chile heat could increase the burn, though the heat is modest here. The tamarind glaze plus a tamarind drink could be too sour or sweet.

What decides it. Taste with the dish at the roast stage and again once the glaze has softened the crust, and compare each drink against the lighter Mexican-style lager.

Butter Chicken & Roasted Poblano Quesadilla

IN DEVELOPMENT

Beer, first idea
Vienna Amber
Zero-proof, first idea
A lassi-inspired drink of cultured dairy, fruit and a little spice, served cold, to echo the sauce and cool the richness.

contrastaciditysweetnesstexturearoma bridge

Why it may work. Toasty malt bridges to the charred chicken, and a sharp or tart drink counters the cream, butter and cheese. A lassi-style drink echoes the sauce in a cooling way.

Alternates, how it could fail, what decides it
Beer, alternate
Hefeweizen
Zero-proof, alternate
A spiced citrus tea with a sharp, dry finish to cut the cream and cheese.

How it could fail. Malt sweetness on a sweet cream sauce could cloy. A dairy drink beside a dairy-rich dish could feel heavy. Yeast spice could clash with the garam masala.

What decides it. Taste each option beside the same wedge, and see whether the drink keeps the second bite as appealing as the first.

Zero-proof is a pairing, not a fallback.

Each non-alcoholic idea is built with the same care as the beer: acid, aroma, texture and a reason. They are categories with a flavour plan, not recipes.

Fresh-fruit, dairy-based and botanical drinks need a food-safety professional to review shelf life, storage and service before anything is served. No fermentation method, health claim or strength claim is made here.

NASHA is a future Indo-Mex brewery and kitchen in Austin, Texas, in development. Nothing is open or for sale, and no site has been chosen. Pictures are concept visualizations or drawings, not photographs of NASHA.

Name, images and allergens

The name was chosen by the founder; legal clearance is pending and nothing here claims trademark ownership. The word NASHA in the header and in some pictures is a temporary typographic placeholder, not a logo. Nasha means intoxication or addiction in Hindi and Urdu: we chose it for the feeling of being drawn in by food, craft and company, we will never present excess as something to admire, and cultural advisors will review the name and our language before launch.

Photographic-style pictures are concept visualizations made with AI tools and edited; drawings are illustrations. None is a photograph of NASHA, its food or its beer (about these images). Dishes are designs for testing, not served food; heat and vegetarian labels are design intent, not a certified allergen or dietary statement. Ask before you eat if you have an allergy. If you drink, drink responsibly; alcohol is for adults of legal drinking age.
